newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha up, support confusing.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha up, support confusing.

text.p: Naphtha prices firmed on Wednesday despite crude losses but traders said they were confused on where the support was coming from.
"It is confusing," a trader said.
Traders said talk on the physical was lacklustre as refiners had yet to fix their August lifting programme.
But fundamentally the region was long with ample prompt supplies.
Similarly, on the paper there was no major buying heard in the market but levels rose by 20 cents per barrel to trade at $20.85 in August.
The contango also disappeared with July, August and September talked at par with a August/September spread traded flat.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) delayed the lifting dates of its high aromatic naphtha (HAN) cargo from Cochin it had tendered to sell, to July 31-August 2 from July 27-29.
"It is to make the product available," a source said.
IOC also on Wednesday issued a fresh tender to sell 25,000 tonnes of natural gas liquids (NGL) lifting July 24-26 from Hazira which closes July 17 and is valid for a day.
IOC's last NGL tender, for a cargo lifting July 12-14 from Hazira, was awarded to a Dutch trader at $37.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Gasoline prices held steady ahead of the award of Taiwan's second-half August reformate import tender which closes late Wednesday and is valid for two days.
Some traders expected offers to be lower than the last award, for August 1-15 delivery at $24.60-24.75 per barrel c-and-f, since Singapore prices have fallen by around $1.00 since.
Only one offer was heard inthe Singapore fob market, for 95-octane unleaded lifting August 3-7, initially at $23.15 per barrel but at $22.90 by the market close.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
